patient_information: A 67-year-old German woman who has lived as an expatriate in Cameroon for the past 4 years.
history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with palpitations at a tropical medicine clinic in Germany and reported transient subcutaneous swellings for the past year; there was no history of fever or constitutional symptoms, and her past medical history was unremarkable; a 24-hour ECG showed paroxysmal supraventricular extrasystoles, and echocardiography revealed a minimal pericardial effusion.
exposure_and_epidemiology: She has lived as an expatriate in Cameroon for 4 years.
vitals: Vital signs are normal, and the patient is afebrile.
physical_exam: There were no visible subcutaneous swellings, heart sounds were clear and regular with no murmurs, and no pathological findings were noted on physical examination.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count showed eosinophilia (14% eosinophils, absolute count 0.868 ×10^9/L); chest radiograph was normal; serology for filarial infections was positive; day-blood samples revealed sheathed microfilariae with a tapered tail characteristic for Loa loa, with a microfilarial count of 1400/mL.
differential_diagnosis: Non-specific urticaria, Calabar swellings in loiasis, cysticercosis, larva currens in Strongyloides stercoralis infection, Mansonella perstans infection, acute schistosomiasis (Katayama syndrome), gnathostomiasis, and sparganosis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with albendazole followed by ivermectin; therapy was tolerated well, the absolute eosinophil count returned to normal, and the microfilarial count declined; follow-up echocardiography 3 months later was normal, the pericardial effusion had resolved, and 24-hour ECG was also normal; palpitations settled with no observed sequelae.

Treatment of Loiasis Matched to Levels of Microfilaraemia (After Boussinesq 2012)
rows: Albendazole 200mg bd for 21 days, followed by ivermectin 150µg/kg stat, then DEC at slowly increasing doses.
Ivermectin 150 µg/kg stat, repeat after 1-3 months until microfilaraemia is <2000 mf/mL, this is followed by treatment with DEC.

DEC: start with low doses of 3-6 mg/d if there are parasites in the blood, 50 mg/d if amicrofilaraemic, divided into 2-3 doses. The dose is doubled every day up to 400 mg/d, still divided into 2-3 doses. Start treatment in hospital. Oral antihistamines or corticosteroids may be useful during the first days of treatment to reduce side effects (arthralgias, pruritus, headache, fever). Several 3- to 4-week courses of DEC administered at intervals of 2-3 weeks may be required to achieve a complete cure.
